newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, Dec hits all-time high.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, Dec hits all-time high.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Thursday in an active session, with spot-December staging a late short covering run to a new all-time high just before it expired, industry sources said.

December surged 42.3 cents late to an all-time spot high of $4.05 per million British thermal units before expiring at $3.901. January settled four cents higher at $3.304 after earlier setting a new benchmark of $3.45. Others ended mixed.
"The longs got out early this afternoon, then weak shorts had to get out at any price," said one East Coast trader, adding Jan should now move up to close the gap with cash.
Traders noted that December bidweek quotes at Henry Hub late Thursday were in the mid-$3.80s, more than 50 cents over the January settlement.
And with cold weather ahead, few expected January to back off significantly near-term despite that the market was technically overbought and due for a pullback after seven consecutive higher closes.

They also said low storage was still a concern, with operators likely to remain cautious about withdrawals early in the season after a steady stream of cold last winter drained stocks to record low levels and spiked prices.
Technical traders pegged January support at today's low of $3.04, with psychological buying likely at $3. Resistance was seen at the ACCESS contract high of $3.63.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices jumped almost 30 cents Thursday to the mid-$3.60s. Midwest pipes were talked more than 40 cents higher in the mid-to-high $3.60s. New York city gate swing gas was pegged in the $4.50-60 area, up more than 50 cents on the day. December gas in New York was quoted in the $5.00 area.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip gained 2.8 cents to $2.472. NYMEX said 89,398 Hub contracts traded, down from Wednesday's record tally of 99,742.

NYMEX December Alberta natgas closed five cents higher at $1.95 after rallying early to a new high of $2.03. Deferred contracts settled up by five to 15 cents. NYMEX said 62 Alberta contracts traded versus 33 on Wednesday.

NYMEX December Permian natgas settled one cent higher at $3.46 after trading early at a new benchmark of $3.50. Deferreds were untraded. NYMEX said 12 Permian lots changed hands compared to no trading on Wednesday.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian December natgas contracts expire Monday, November 25.

On the KCBT, December, which set a new high Thursday of $4.00, finished 2.8 cents higher at $3.65, while forward months ended mixed. The East/West spread widened 24.6 cents to 25.1 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 905 contracts traded, down from Wednesday's total of 1,001.
KCBT December natgas expires Friday, November 22.
